youtube.title: LESTER BRYANT
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with Lester Bryant, Energy spokesperson for the New Zealand Outdoors and Freedom Party, about escalating tensions in the Middle East and the potential fallout for global oil supply. Lester warns that disruption in the Strait of Hormuz could severely impact fuel availability, with New Zealand especially vulnerable due to its reliance on imported energy and geographic isolation. Also check out out Paul's interview with petrochemical industry veteran Harvey Weake To help you get prepared check out: Rodney Hide's interview with Carolyn Eichler – founder of Prepper Kiwi on gardening, hunting and basic survival skills Also: Simon Fleck's practical tips for prepping on a budget and with limited space and Simon Fleck's pointers for being prepared for natural disasters LINC preparedness on creating an independent CB radio network in NZ

youtube.title: DEB CUNLIFFE
youtube.summary: Deb Cunliffe, President of the Nurses Collective NZ joins Paul Brennan to discuss the Second Covid Inquiry report and how it has failed in its mandate to learn lessons and interrogate the evidence and most importantly the examine the lack of ethics, extent of harm and lack of transparency around the Covid response. Deb says the report treats moral injury as emotional fallout, rather than evidence of systemic failure by decision-makers. Earlier this month, the collective sent an open letter to the commissioners expressing deep disappointment with the findings.

youtube.title: SUE GREY
youtube.summary: Lawyer Sue Grey returns to update Paul Brennan on the final day of Dr Bernard Conlon’s disciplinary tribunal in Rotorua, brought by the Medical Council of New Zealand. She describes a packed venue overwhelmingly there in support and recounts how the Professional Conduct Committee presented its case. The Tribunal's decision is expected early next week.

youtube.title: LEGAL HUB
youtube.summary: Katie Ashby-Koppens joins Paul Brennan for a Legal Hub catch-up on New Zealand’s decision to reject proposed WHO international health regulation changes, framing it as a win for national sovereignty. Katie credits persistent public pressure and political backing, noting the decision came down to maintaining domestic control over health responses.

youtube.title: THE BRENNAN BAROMETER
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan’s end-of-week Barometer dissects the emotional fallout from Chris Hipkins’ public response to personal allegations, questioning whether the display was genuine or calculated. He contrasts media framing with his own scepticism, before widening the lens to critique celebrity-style political branding through glossy magazine culture.

youtube.title: WEEKLY ROUNDUP
youtube.summary: Dieuwe De Boer and William McGimpsey discuss New Zealand’s energy resilience during the fuel supply crisis linked to the Iran war, along with immigration, economic growth, political trust, and shifting foreign relations with the US and China.

youtube.title: FREDDIE PONTON
youtube.summary: Freddie Ponton, Global Affairs editor at 21st Century Wire, joins RCR to discuss updates on the Iran War, which he characterises as a war of survival for Iran. They discuss the Strait of Hormuz being closed to US allies and the Israeli strike on the South Pars gas field as a major escalation of the war, with significant impacts on Iran's civilian population. However, Ponton says this will only firm up the resolve of the Iranians, as seen in the retaliatory attack on energy security infrastructure in Qatar, which will have knock-on effects for fuel supplies internationally. Discover more from 21st Century Wire or find them on X Follow Freddie on X

youtube.title: RIDING SHOTGUN
youtube.summary: This week on Riding Shotgun , Rachel Stewart notes that the Oscars’ viewership has fallen sharply from around 50 million in 2000 to under 18 million today. While industry figures attribute this to changing viewing habits, she argues the deeper cause is public disengagement driven by perceptions of Hollywood elitism, political messaging, and insider influence over awards. Discover more from Rachel on Substack and X

youtube.title: RACHEL’S MAILBAG
youtube.summary: Listeners reflect on the lasting scars of COVID-era policies, sharing deeply personal stories of separation, job loss, medical concerns, and grief. The messages reveal a common thread of disillusionment, with many questioning official narratives and expressing a desire for accountability, recognition, and, for some, long-overdue apologies. Text your feedback to 2057 or email inbox@rcr.media

youtube.title: AIDAN MCLINDON
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with politician Aidan McLindon about a turbulent week in Australia, with surging fuel prices and panic buying. They also discuss Victoria’s proposed fee to visit the 12 Apostles, the rise of One Nation in South Australia, unrest inside Victorian Labor, and warnings that Cyclone Narelle could hit far north Queensland hard. For more information on the Aligned Council of Australia

youtube.title: WEDNESDAY WEBINARS
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan is joined by independent journalist and freelance writer Penny Marie and RCR host Nathan Smith for a wide-ranging webinar on New Zealand politics, media influence, public distrust, and the long shadow of COVID. They argue polls often shape opinion as much as reflect it, criticise mainstream media framing on issues from Chris Hipkins to the Middle East, and say the health system still rewards sickness over prevention. For more information: NZDSOS Rumble Channel: Gardasil Documentary Penny Marie Propaganda in Hindsight Part 1 Penny Marie Propaganda in Hindsight Part 2 Discover more from Penny Marie on her website , YouTube and X Or check out Let Kids be Kids Follow Nathan Smith on Substack

youtube.title: MEDIA MATTERS
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke and Marty Gibson discuss New Zealand rejecting the WHO’s pandemic rule changes, the lingering fallout of the Royal Commission report and the media’s framing of Chris Hipkins’ personal drama. They argue establishment outlets are protecting political favourites while missing the bigger questions around accountability, sovereignty and public trust. For more information: Winston Peters Facebook Post on IHR Amendments NZ Herald: Mathew Hooton article: Royal Commission report – why Chris Hipkins must apologise to Aucklanders NZ Herald: Bruce Cotteril: TVNZ has lost its way and the public deserves better Penny Marie X Post on United Nations Sustainable Development Goals Leighton Smith Podcast #319 – March 11th 2026 – Robert MacCulloch NZ Herald: Top US Counterterrorism official Joe Kent resigns in opposition to Iran war Fiona Rose Diamond X Post

youtube.title: KEN TURNER
youtube.summary: Auckland City Councillor Ken Turner joins Paul Brennan to discuss how intensification plans are being progressed despite a $4 million consultation process being incomplete with many submissions yet to be analysed. Plan Change 120 will introduce high rise apartment blocks to parts of Auckland where residents are opposed to them. He draws strong parallels between the plan change and the 15 minute cities concept.

youtube.title: WINSTON PETERS
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan is rejoined by Winston Peters to discuss a sweeping mix from Fonterra’s direction and New Zealand’s fuel vulnerability to tensions with China and defence ties with Australia. Peters defends rejecting the WHO pandemic changes as a matter of sovereignty and signals more action to come on COVID accountability.

youtube.title: MAREE’S MAILBAG
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke’s latest mailbag ranges from distrust of legacy media; to concerns over online censorship to anguished reflections on vaccine harm and the lasting bitterness of the COVID era. Maree highlights growing backlash against ideological capture in medical, nursing and midwifery councils and touches on RCR’s treatment in an AUT paper.
